methodology: Each label rests on a checkable public fact, not on judgement. 'authentic' entries are official institutional accounts (the organisation verifies its own identity). 'inauthentic' entries must carry a source_ref pointing at an entry in `sources`, or they are excluded from scoring by validate_benchmark_labels(). No inauthentic handles are shipped in this file: platform takedowns remove the accounts, so names have to be imported from the cited datasets rather than recalled from memory.

run_requirements.note: Scoring this set needs one collection run per account. The 4 seed entries require ~56 provider credits, which exceeds the balance available when this file was written. The set is therefore NOT yet scored and no accuracy figure exists.

sources.name: Meta Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior reports
sources.what_it_gives: Named networks with account/page handle lists and the behaviour that caused removal.
sources.limitation: Handles are deleted at takedown, so they can no longer be collected. Useful for behaviour taxonomy and for testing whether the detector flags the described patterns, not for live scoring.
sources.license_note: Public company statements; cite the report date in label_source.

sources.name: EU DSA Transparency Database (statements of reasons)
sources.what_it_gives: Machine-readable decisions per content/account, including account suspensions with a stated category and legal ground.
sources.limitation: Bulk exports are large and mostly content-level; account-level rows need filtering by decision_ground and decision_visibility.
sources.license_note: Published under DSA Art. 24; CC-BY-style reuse with attribution to the platform statement.

sources.name: Twibot-20 labelled Twitter bot dataset
sources.what_it_gives: Account-level human/bot labels with the annotation method and inter-annotator agreement recorded.
sources.limitation: Twitter accounts from the 2020 crawl; many are suspended or renamed, so collection will fail for a share of rows. Report the collection success rate with any score.
sources.license_note: Research dataset - check its LICENSE before redistributing handles; keep only ids in this repo.

sources.name: Botometer (OSoMe, Indiana University) - historical reference implementation
sources.what_it_gives: A published scoring method whose thresholds can be compared against ours.
sources.limitation: Service availability has changed over time and its labels are model output, not ground truth. Use as a comparison baseline, never as a label source.
sources.license_note: Cite the accompanying paper when comparing.

harvest_rules: An 'inauthentic' label needs a source_ref AND the platform's own stated reason for the action. 'Looks like a bot to me' is not a label.
Record the collection date of the cited export; a suspended account proves nothing about today's account with the same handle.
Never re-collect an account that was removed for harassment or abuse: the posts are victims' content and the account is not consenting.
Keep only profile ids and the citation in this file - no post text, no personal data, from the source dataset.

accounts.notes: Verified news organisation publishing under its own brand.
Analysed across tasks 7-16; consistent first-person Bengali posting history, no coordination evidence. Labelled authentic by manual review - a weak label source, recorded as such.

exclusions: No 'inauthentic' examples are shipped. Add rows with `is_inauthentic: true`, a `source_ref` naming an id from `sources`, and the platform's stated reason; validate_benchmark_labels() drops uncited rows instead of guessing.
